extracted.intended_audience: authors and agents proposing books on gardening, horticulture, natural history, and related trade nonfiction
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for preparing and submitting a trade nonfiction book proposal to Timber Press (Workman Publishing), focused on gardening, horticulture, natural history, garden literature, and field guides. Specifies required proposal components, sample materials, marketing information, and submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject fit / topical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Timber Press is devoted to sharing the wonders of the natural world by publishing books from experts in the fields of gardening, horticulture, and natural history. Our list includes gardening how-to, garden design, popular science, nature, garden literature, and both regional and national field guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be for books within these areas; Timber Press considers new book ideas from authors and agents. Ensure your topic aligns with the imprint's areas of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview (uniqueness, approach, audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell us what is unique about your book and why we should publish it. Discuss your overall approach and the organization of the book. Define your intended audience and explain why the book will appeal to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the book's unique selling points, its structure/organization, and clearly define and justify the target reader. Emphasize why Timber Press should publish this project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents and chapter-by-chapter description
rubrics_metrics.description: List all chapters, along with any front matter (introduction, preface) and back matter (appendices, charts, references, bibliography, index). Briefly describe what is contained in each chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, complete TOC including front/back matter; include concise descriptions for each chapter to convey scope and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative sample chapter (length requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a representative sample chapter of no more than 10 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a chapter that best demonstrates voice, expertise, and the book’s approach. Keep sample chapter at or under 10 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize your familiarity with the subject and explain why you are qualified to write the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant expertise, credentials, professional experience, publications, speaking history, and any other qualifications that establish authority on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales and marketing considerations / author platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly list any specific aspects of the book that will help Timber Press in its sales and marketing efforts. Describe your marketing platform (how your social media and professional activities and contacts will aid the promotion of the book). If you give lectures or workshops, include a summary of your activities for the past year. Please describe your current social media outreach with any applicable links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail tangible marketing assets: social media metrics and links, mailing lists, media contacts, speaking/teaching engagements (with recent activity), and other promotional channels. Explain how these will support book sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing / comparable titles
rubrics_metrics.description: List any books published in the past five years that address the same subject as your book. Describe how your book differs from or is superior to these competing titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each comparable title include publisher, publication date, price, and Amazon ranking. Use this analysis to demonstrate distinction and market need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length estimate and art/illustration plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an estimated word count for your completed manuscript and a general art plan including photos, illustrations, maps, graphs, and/or diagrams that you feel are necessary to convey your ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If working with a professional photographer, explain why he or she is well suited to the project. Include sample images or a link to the photographer’s website. Be specific about types/amounts of art and how they support the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are only accepted via email. Please direct your proposal to editorial@timberpress.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission channel exactly (email to the given address). Note Timber Press is an imprint of Workman Publishing; see the publisher's submissions page for other imprints or broader submission policies.
